SMTO-EXE-0230 — Other Docker containers already use this project name

GUID: 91eb7b28-f5b8-5cc5-a692-f82835a9222d
Slug: docker-compose-project-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Containers on the Gateway computer already use this Compose project name, but they were started from a different folder, set of files or options. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't change another project. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the Docker Compose projects on that Gateway, and note the folder and files the project with this name uses. SMTO only acts on containers whose recorded folder and files match your request.
  2. If it's your project, ask again using exactly that folder, the same Compose files in the same order, and the same profiles it was started with. Matching every one of those details proves the containers belong to the project you mean.
  3. If it's a different project, choose a new, unique project name for yours. A different name keeps your containers apart from the other project's.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the project and shows its containers or services without this warning.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Docker on that computer. Don't stop or remove the other project's containers to get around this; they may belong to someone else's work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Before a Compose action, existing containers labeled with the requested com.docker.compose.project name carried an SMTO identity digest, working_dir or config_files label that does not match the requested project inputs.

What this means

  • Current containers share the requested Compose project name but their recorded working-directory/config-file identity or stored identity digest does not match the request. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Current containers share the requested Compose project name but their recorded working-directory/config-file identity or stored identity digest does not match the request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare project name, absolute working directory, ordered config files, profiles and ownership labels.

How to fix it

  • Inspect containers carrying the com.docker.compose.project label for this name and compare their io.smto.compose.identity, working_dir and config_files labels with the request. Either resend the exact working_dir, files, project_name and profiles that created them, or choose a unique project_name; never act on same-name containers from another project.
  • Select the exact recorded project inputs and ownership; do not act on same-name containers from another project.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Current containers match the exact intended project identity before any project mutation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
